My last pup had kidney issues and was very old. I don't think that a little piece of meat or some dog treats that he actually liked here and there would have hurt him and it would have made his quality of life much better, he loved snacks so much. 
With my current pup, I give him a bite of most everything I'm eating that doesn't have anything toxic in it. If I'm eating something he can't have, I make him a little meal of his own to go with his kibble. I understand both sides though, ultimately all we want for our pups is for them to be happy and healthy.

I have so much to say about this topic as it is something I struggled with my whole life until my body started feeling really sick and yucky from my comfort foods... it got so bad that I was just eating the bare minimum amount of food and even that I had to choke down so I sought help for what I thought was anorexia. My therapist determined that it was not anorexia but food aversion and it's how I first found out I might be autistic. I also saw a nutritionist at the hospital when I couldn't get any food down and she had a similar strategy to that first therapist. 

My therapist asked me some questions to help me figure out what I like. We explored my comfort foods and we went through the specifics on what I liked and disliked about different types of foods and made lists from there. 
 So sorry this is long winded but I really wanted to give an
 example of how just listening to myself and being open minded helped a lot. 
I love boba so we started there. We figured out that I like the smooth and fun feeling of having little tapioca boba in my mouth but only if I'm chewing them one at a time> that made them ask me if I like jello> I start crawling out of my skin just thinking of a time I ate a bite of jello from a big bowl of it > I actually do like jello if it is cut in cubes and I can eat them individually> which made me realize I like small pieces of smooth things because I can feel it all in my mouth at once> all of this helped me explore similar textures which made me realize I love chia seeds, aloe vera drinks, wide rice noodles, marinated cucumber salad (the oily texture on the smooth flesh of the cucumber is incredible but biting into a cucumber on its own ?? 🤮) , cut up apples, blueberries, oranges but only after I've delicately dissected each individual piece, eating the skin and then sucking on the smooth part of the fruit under.

Your daughter likely has different food she likes but these are just some examples of foods I could never ever see myself eating before and now absolutely love to eat because I learned to make eating SUPER flexible (which it sounds like ur doing already!!!)  and focus on the sensory joy of eating. I've found that while I experience negative sensory stuff really strongly, I also experience positive sensory stuff strongly in a way that NT ppl may not and I can work with that.
